_doc.purpose: Maps detector coder-IDs to plain-English pattern names + family + description for use in user-facing memory ('you understand X', 'you missed Y again'). Authored 2026-05-23 by Claude as v1 starters per Mohit's P1; voice tuning expected once he reviews in the UI.
_doc.audience: 600-1500 rated players — no jargon (no 'fianchetto', 'prophylaxis', 'zwischenzug'). Name the square / the idea instead.

schema.pattern_id: Stable snake_case key. Used in user_pattern_events docs as the pattern reference. NEVER renamed once shipped — only the human_name/description/family fields are tunable.
schema.human_name: Short coach-voice name, 3-6 words. What you'd say to a student.
schema.short_description: One sentence in coach voice. WHY it matters or WHAT it does, not just what it is.
schema.family: Tactical/positional grouping. Used to roll up related patterns in insights ('you handle the Légal's family well — 4/5 hits').
schema.example_fen: Canonical example position. Optional — null means Mohit will fill from a known game later.
schema.canonical_concept_id: Optional existing caption_principles ID. New events use it as concept_id; pattern_id remains the stable legacy alias.

coach_memory_bridge.what: coach_memory.learning.skills stores skill ids in an older vocabulary than the 238 curriculum concept ids. Entries with family 'coach_memory alias' carry canonical_concept_id and ARE that concept. Entries with family 'coach_memory lesson' carry teaches_concept_id: a finished lesson is attendance, not evidence the player holds the concept, so it must never be read as a concept observation.
coach_memory_bridge.authority: A record's own skill_type field decides its kind. See services/personal_teaching_profile.skill_kind.
coach_memory_bridge.measured: 2026-09-13, all 8,166 production skill records: 7,910 openings, 113 concepts across 11 ids, 143 lesson records.

deliberately_unmapped.endgame_philidor: The Philidor third-rank rook defence has no counterpart among the 238 curriculum concepts. A curriculum gap, not a naming gap.
deliberately_unmapped.mate_kq_vs_k: Basic K+Q mate is absent from the 238 curriculum concepts.
deliberately_unmapped.mate_kr_vs_k: Basic K+R mate is absent from the 238 curriculum concepts.
deliberately_unmapped.italian_game_fried_liver_attack: A trap lesson -- playing the Fried Liver rather than defending it. Traps have no concept counterpart; the DEFENCE does, and defend_fried_liver maps to OP_F2_F7_STRIKE.
deliberately_unmapped.queens_gambit_elephant_trap: A trap lesson. The Elephant Trap punishes 5.Nxd5 in the Queen's Gambit Declined; the curriculum has no concept for a specific opening trap, and the general idea it rests on (a pinned knight) is already reachable through the pin alias.
deliberately_unmapped.trap_set_italian: A trap lesson: setting a trap in the Italian. The curriculum carries no trap concepts at all, and 'setting a trap' is a choice a player makes, not a fundamental the system measures.

coach_memory_bridge.umbrella: Entries with family 'coach_memory umbrella' carry umbrella_concept_ids: the stored id names a GROUP of concepts, so a lookup for any concept in the group reaches that history. This is broader than an exact alias and concept_aliases(cid, exact_only=True) excludes it, so a consumer that needs a precise match can still ask for one.

missed_mate.short_description: There was a forced mating sequence — every opponent reply loses.

missed_piece.short_description: A clean way to win a knight, bishop, rook, or queen — the engine saw it cleanly.

clearance_for_attack.human_name: Open the line so your piece attacks
clearance_for_attack.short_description: Move a piece out of the way so another of yours has a direct shot at the king or a key square.

clearance_then_check.short_description: Sacrifice a knight (or pawn) to open the line so your queen can deliver check on the next move.

queen_fork_capture_with_check.short_description: Queen move that grabs material and checks the king on the same turn.

queen_fork.short_description: Queen move that attacks the king and another loose piece at once.

attack_with_tempo.short_description: Hit an enemy piece with a move that also improves yours — opponent has to react.

endgame_loose_pawn_capture.short_description: In the endgame, your active piece grabs an opponent pawn that has no defender.

endgame_loose_pawn_attack.short_description: In the endgame, move an active piece next to an opponent pawn that has no defender — you can grab it next.

un_developing.short_description: Moving a developed piece back to its starting square wastes a tempo — usually a better move exists.

defensive_pawn_push.human_name: Don't push wing pawns when you should be developing
defensive_pawn_push.short_description: Slow wing pawn moves (a3, h6) cost time when the position is asking for a piece to come out.

knight_outpost.human_name: Knight to a defended central square
knight_outpost.short_description: Park a knight on a central square that's protected by your own pawn and can't be kicked away — a long-term home.

stop_opp_pawn.human_name: Block opponent's pawn before it pushes
stop_opp_pawn.short_description: Get a piece or pawn in front of opponent's pawn so they can't keep pushing it into your camp.

active_defense.short_description: A move that protects your threatened piece AND hits something of theirs — turns defense into pressure.

same_piece_better_square.short_description: Same piece type you moved, but to a square where it hits more loose targets at once.

discovered_vacating_check.human_name: Move gives check; vacated square opens attack
discovered_vacating_check.short_description: Move a piece to check the king while the square it leaves opens a line for another of yours to hit a loose target.

knight_on_rim.human_name: Avoid knight on the rim in the opening
knight_on_rim.short_description: Knights on the a- or h-file in the opening attack very few squares — develop toward the center instead.

pawn_kicks_piece.human_name: Pawn push that kicks an enemy piece
pawn_kicks_piece.short_description: Pawn move that attacks an enemy piece, forcing it to retreat — gains time.

blocked_own_pawn.short_description: A piece move that sits where your own pawn needed to advance — usually push the pawn first.

king_pawn_lifted.human_name: Attack the weak square in front of the king
king_pawn_lifted.short_description: Opponent's f- or g-pawn moved off its starting square, leaving a weak point in front of the king — pile up there.

trap_punishment.short_description: Opponent reached a setup that's part of a known trap; the engine's move is the textbook refutation.

pre_move_check.human_name: Scan the opponent's checks, captures and threats before you commit — that scan is literally what this habit is.
pre_move_check.short_description: Scan the opponent's checks, captures and threats before you commit — that scan is literally what this habit is.
pre_move_check.why_this_concept: The pre-move check IS the checks/captures/threats sweep. Same act, two names.

defend_fried_liver.human_name: Hold f7 when the knight jumps to g5.
defend_fried_liver.short_description: Hold f7 when the knight jumps to g5.
defend_fried_liver.why_this_concept: The Fried Liver is Nxf7 after 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5 6.Nxf7. Defending it is defending the f7 strike — that is the same motif, not a related one.

defend_scholars_mate.human_name: Stop the early mate on f7.
defend_scholars_mate.short_description: Stop the early mate on f7.
defend_scholars_mate.why_this_concept: Scholar's mate is Qxf7# supported by Bc4 — the mate lands ON f7, so the square is the concept. OP_QUEEN_OUT_EARLY is the co-cause (the queen that delivers it gets chased once f7 holds), but f7 is what the defender guards.

free_piece_capture.human_name: Take the piece that is defended by nothing.
free_piece_capture.short_description: Take the piece that is defended by nothing.
free_piece_capture.why_this_concept: Same motif seen from the winning side: the piece is hanging, you collect it. One concept, two vantage points — not two weaknesses.

fork.human_name: One piece attacking two things at once.
fork.short_description: One piece attacking two things at once.
fork.why_this_concept: Exact identity. knight_fork is the knight-specific sub-case; the bare `fork` record names no piece, so it maps to the general pattern.

pin.human_name: A piece that cannot move without exposing something behind it.
pin.short_description: A piece that cannot move without exposing something behind it.

opponent_threat.human_name: Ask what the opponent's last move changed.
opponent_threat.short_description: Ask what the opponent's last move changed.
opponent_threat.why_this_concept: Spotting the opponent's threat is reading what their move altered — the curriculum states the habit as the question, the memory states it as the object.

endgame_opposition.why_this_concept: endgames.json key `opposition`, stored with the endgame_ prefix.

endgame_rule_of_square.human_name: Whether the king catches the running pawn.
endgame_rule_of_square.short_description: Whether the king catches the running pawn.
endgame_rule_of_square.why_this_concept: endgames.json key `rule_of_square`, stored with the endgame_ prefix.

opening_principles.human_name: Opening principles, worked as one habit.
opening_principles.short_description: Opening principles, worked as one habit.
opening_principles.why_this_concept: The habit is 'develop your pieces, take the centre, castle' -- exactly these three concepts. It names the group, so it resolves to the group. The six golden_opening_principle_* ids were NOT used: they are filler, sharing one generic message with 79 other ids.

king_pawn_endgame.why_this_concept: A whole class of ending, not one idea. The concepts inside it are the opposition, the passed pawn, the active king and the rule of the square.

conversion.human_name: Turning a won position into a win.
conversion.short_description: Turning a won position into a win.
conversion.why_this_concept: Converting an advantage is endgame technique: push the passed pawn, activate the king, keep the rook active. One record, so the group is the honest answer -- narrowing it to a single concept would invent detail the record does not carry.
